theme: 3 terms on copies that stay independent: copies that never affect each other, sharing storage until a change, and checking if a reference is the only one

terms.definition: A behavior where every copy of a value is independent, so changing one copy never changes another.
terms.example: Arrays have Value Semantics, so changing `b` won't touch `a`.
terms.code:
var a = [1, 2]
var b = a
b.append(3)
print(a)
print(b)

terms.definition: An optimization where copies share the same storage until one of them is changed.
terms.example: Copying the big array is cheap, thanks to Copy-on-Write.
terms.code:
var a = [1, 2, 3]
var b = a      // shares storage, no copy
b[0] = 9       // copies now, then changes
print(a, b)

terms.definition: A Swift function that returns true when only one strong reference points to a class instance.
terms.example: Check isKnownUniquelyReferenced before you write to the shared buffer.

quizzes.question: What function tells you if only one strong reference points to a class instance?
In this code, what behavior keeps `a` as `[1, 2]` after `b` changes?
quizzes.code:
var a = [1, 2]
var b = a
b.append(3)

quizzes.question: What do you call sharing storage between copies until one of them changes?

landscape.hook: Can you explain copy-on-write in English?

dialogue.title: Why did a change too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `Counter` is a struct, but changing `b` changed `a` too!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Look inside. `box` is a class, so both copies share it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So my struct doesn't have Value Semantics anymore?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Value Semantics means each copy changes on its own.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should I copy `box` every time I copy `Counter`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's slow. Use Copy-on-Write: share it, and copy only when someone writes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I know when to copy?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Call isKnownUniquelyReferenced on `box` before you change it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And if it returns false, I make a new `Box` first?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. If isKnownUniquelyReferenced says true, nobody else shares it, so just write.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Copy-on-Write keeps Value Semantics and stays fast.
Value Semantics means a copy never changes the original.
